notes: Five skill/task inputs across difficulties. The output must be usable by the runtime unchanged — every generated question is turned into a QuestionSpec and validated against the Phase-0 contract, so 'good question' includes 'has an authored fallback probe and a clarify line', because those are what stop a rejected follow-up becoming silence.

skills.name: De-escalation
skills.assessment_scope: Holding a line under pressure without either capitulating or escalating the conflict.

tasks.description: Take a call from a customer who is shouting about a repeated failure and has already been transferred twice
tasks.outcome: The customer leaves with the problem owned and a named next step.

skills.name: Troubleshooting
skills.assessment_scope: Narrowing a vague report to a cause, and knowing when to stop guessing.

tasks.description: Diagnose a customer report of 'the dashboard isn't loading' with no error message and no reproduction steps
tasks.outcome: Issues are escalated with enough context that nobody has to start again.

skills.name: Customer empathy
skills.assessment_scope: Reading how a customer feels and acting on it before explaining.

tasks.description: Handle a customer whose team was locked out mid-shift by a failed renewal
tasks.outcome: Customers leave with their problem solved and their time respected.

cases.notes: The opening question a candidate meets. It must be answerable by someone who is nervous and has not warmed up yet — an 'easy' question that is actually a hard scenario is how an interview loses a good candidate in the first ninety seconds.

skills.name: Coaching
skills.assessment_scope: Improving someone else's performance through specific, early feedback.

skills.name: Queue prioritisation
skills.assessment_scope: Deciding what waits when everything is urgent.

tasks.description: Coach an agent through their first hard escalation and give feedback afterwards
tasks.outcome: Agents handle harder work over time without the lead taking it over.

tasks.description: Rebalance the queue during a backlog when first response time is slipping
tasks.outcome: The queue stays inside its response target on the tickets that matter most.

cases.notes: Two skills, two tasks. Each question must map to exactly one skill — a question that assesses both cannot be scored against either.

skills.name: Designing for correctness under failure
skills.assessment_scope: Reasoning about partial failure, idempotency and the cost asymmetry between error types.

tasks.description: Design idempotent payment capture so a retried request cannot double-charge a customer
tasks.outcome: No customer is charged twice, and no successful payment is silently lost.

cases.notes: Spoken aloud, not read. A question a candidate has to hold four clauses of in their head is a memory test.
